goal_summary: Bounded source investigation and primary-literature curation of five uncurated IMA-approved critical-element mineral species from the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC Master List with open-access type descriptions in European Journal of Mineralogy (volumes 32, 36, and 38).

curated_sources_and_records.name: Niasite
type_specimens: Holotype AMNH 17956 (American Museum of Natural History, New York; three major fragments and numerous smaller ones including 10 pieces mounted on two acrylic discs; also holotype of johanngeorgenstadtite)
Cotype LACMNH 74203 (Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County; 5 fragments mounted on a glass slide, ex-Mark Feinglos collection, originally from matrix of AMNH 17956)

primary_source.citation: Kampf AR, Nash BP, Plášil J, Smith JB, Feinglos MN (2020) Niasite and johanngeorgenstadtite, Ni2+4.5(AsO4)3 dimorphs from Johanngeorgenstadt, Germany. European Journal of Mineralogy 32:373-385

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Table 3 (p. 380) prints crystal dimensions for niasite as '35 mm x 30 mm x 20 mm' via a mm-for-um unit typo; Section 6 prose (p. 377) gives the true dimensions 35 um x 30 um x 20 um.

Table 6a (p. 383) prints the O1 bond-valence sum as 1.99 v.u., whereas the printed bond-valence contributions 0.39 (Ni1) + 0.35 (Ni2) + 1.24 (As2) sum arithmetically to 1.98 v.u. due to unrounded summation.
Section 6 prose (p. 377) spells the dimorph 'johanngeorgenstatite' (missing the second 'd') once.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Manganoschafarzikite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Hindenburg working (~150 m level), Långban Fe-Mn skarn deposit (59.85° N, 14.26° E), Filipstad district, Värmland Province, Sweden
type_specimens: Holotype GEO-NRM 19339699 (Department of Geosciences, Swedish Museum of Natural History, Stockholm)
Crystal fragment KNR 44410 (Natural History Museum, University of Oslo)

primary_source.citation: Holtstam D, Langhof J, Friis H, Karlsson A, Erambert M (2024) Igelströmite, Fe3+(Sb3+Pb2+)O4, and manganoschafarzikite, Mn2+Sb3+2O4, two new members of the newly established minium group, from the Långban Mn-Fe deposit, Värmland, Sweden. European Journal of Mineralogy 36:311-322

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 5.2 (p. 315) prints the refined powder XRD unit-cell volume for manganoschafarzikite as V = 442.23(5) Å3, whereas a = 8.6273(5) Å and c = 5.9683(5) Å yield a^2 * c = 444.22(5) Å3.
Section 6.1 prints the weak Sb-O-Sb bending Raman band as 402 cm-1 on p. 315 vs 405 cm-1 on p. 316 and in Fig. 3.
Table 10 (p. 318) prints the mean Mn-O octahedral distance as 2.147 Å whereas Section 7.1 prose (p. 318) prints 2.146 Å (exact arithmetic mean 2.1465 Å).
Section 3 (p. 313) prints the reflectance spectral window as '400-70 nm range' for 400-700 nm, and Section 5.1 (p. 314) prints the MoKalpha wavelength as 'lambda = 0.71703 Å' for 0.71073 Å.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Erzwiesite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Unnamed prospect at 2390 m a.s.l. west of 'Blei Beul' ('Beim Bleibau'), Erzwies mining area, Gastein Valley, Hohe Tauern, Salzburg Province, Austria (47°05'40" N, 13°02'15" E)
type_specimens: Holotype NHMW O 2407 (Natural History Museum Vienna, Austria)

primary_source.citation: Topa D, Makovicky E, Putz H, Paar WH, Zagler G (2026) Erzwiesite, Ag8Pb12Bi16S40, the natural orthorhombic N = 8 member of the lillianite homologous series. European Journal of Mineralogy 38:237-247

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 4 (p. 241) and Table 2 column IF (p. 242) print the ideal wt% composition for Ag8Pb12Bi16S40 as Ag 10.82, Pb 31.76, Bi 41.92, S 16.08, total 100.00 wt%, whereas the arithmetic sum of those four rounded weight percentages is 100.58 wt%.
Abstract (p. 237) prints Dcalc = 7.075 g/cm3 whereas Section 3 (p. 240) prints Dcalc = 7.045 g/cm3 (empirical formula) and 7.074 g/cm3 (structural formula).

Section 5 (p. 242, right column) contains a copy-paste typo reading 'for the available crystal from Madoc' carried over from the companion lopatkaite paper, and Fig. 8 caption (p. 244) twice spells the mineral 'erwiesite'.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Kenoargentotetrahedrite-(Zn)
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Yindongpo gold deposit, Weishancheng Au-Ag-Pb-Zn ore belt, Tongbai County, Nanyang City, Henan Province, China (32°33'02" N, 113°25'25" E)
type_specimens: Holotype M16112 (Geological Museum of China, Beijing)

primary_source.citation: Qu K, Sima X, Gu X, Sun W, Fan G, Yang Z, Wang Y (2024) Kenoargentotetrahedrite-(Zn), [Ag6]4+(Cu4Zn2)Sb4S12□, a new member of the tetrahedrite group from the Yindongpo Au deposit, China. European Journal of Mineralogy 36:397-409

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 5 prose on p. 401 writes the doubled M(2b) site occupancy as '0.436(9) apfu', whereas 2 x 0.219(9) = 0.438(9) apfu as printed on p. 402 (coupled with S(2) occupancy 0.438(19) at 2a).
Table 2 (p. 401) bolds seven reflections including 1.909 Å (Imeas = 5; 1 2 5), while two other reflections at 2.792 Å (1 2 3) and 2.456 Å (0 3 3) also have Imeas = 5.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Lopatkaite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Taylor Pit, Lot 13, Concession XIV, Huntingdon Township, Madoc area, Hastings County, Ontario, Canada
type_specimens: Holotype NHMW O 3954 (Natural History Museum Vienna, Austria; transferred from Mineralogical Museum of the University of Salzburg, former catalogue no. 15008)

primary_source.citation: Topa D, Makovicky E, Putz H, Zagler G (2026) Lopatkaite, a new mineral from Taylor Pit, Madoc, Ontario, Canada. European Journal of Mineralogy 38:217-229

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Table 5 (p. 223) prints the bond-valence sum (BVS) for site (Pb,Sb)4 without a decimal point as '2128' for 2.128 v.u.

Table 2 (p. 220) prints the Group 5 mean analytical total as 100.46 wt% (arithmetic sum of rounded means 57.81 + 20.03 + 3.53 + 19.08 = 100.45 wt%) and Group 6 mean total as 99.77 wt% (arithmetic sum 99.76 wt%).
